definition: MobileNet is a family of convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures designed for image classification, object detection, and other computer vision tasks.
details: They are designed for small size, low latency, and low power consumption, making them suitable for on-device inference and edge computing on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones and embedded systems. They were originally designed to be run efficiently on mobile devices with TensorFlow Lite. The need for efficient deep learning models on mobile devices led researchers at Google to develop MobileNet. As of June 2025, the family has five versions, each improving upon the previous one in terms of performance and efficiency.

explainer.lead: MobileNet is a family of convolutional neural network architectures designed for image classification, object detection and other computer vision tasks. It matters because it targets small size, low latency and low power, enabling on-device inference where compute and battery are limited.

tiers.eli5: It's a vision model built to be small and fast enough to run on a phone instead of a big server.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers deploy MobileNet variants on phones and embedded systems, typically via TensorFlow Lite, when they need real-time vision within tight memory and power budgets. The pitfall is that the efficiency gains come with reduced accuracy versus larger models, which can hurt on hard images.
tiers.paperLevel: A family of CNN architectures optimised for small size, low latency and low power consumption, suited to edge computing and on-device inference. As of June 2025 the family has five versions, each improving on the previous one.

explainer.example: A phone app might run a MobileNet model on the camera feed to detect objects in real time without sending frames to a server.
